title: Warehouse throughput collapse
case_study: A regional distribution centre saw order throughput fall 34% over six weeks with headcount unchanged and inbound volume flat. The floor supervisor blames a new pick-path algorithm; the vendor blames seasonal SKU mix. No A/B window was held before rollout and the prior algorithm was decommissioned.

title: Duplicate refunds after migration
case_study: Following a payments migration, 1,180 customers received a refund twice within 48 hours because the reconciliation job ran against the legacy ledger for two days after cutover. Its cron entry was never repointed. Finance caught it on the daily variance report.

title: Clinic no-show rate spike
case_study: An outpatient clinic's no-show rate rose from 8% to 21% after switching reminder vendors. The new vendor sends SMS two days ahead at 09:00; the old one sent the evening before. Online-only booking launched the same month and the patient mix shifted younger.

title: Contractor invoice mismatch
case_study: A facilities contractor invoiced 2,400 hours in a month where badge data shows 1,650 on site. The contract permits off-site preparation, which is not badge-tracked and has never been itemised. Timesheets are signed by a manager who left during the period under review.

title: Model drift in fraud screening
case_study: A fraud-screening model's precision fell from 0.91 to 0.68 in one quarter while recall held steady, with no code or threshold change deployed. A new merchant category onboarded in the same quarter contributes 12% of volume. The training set is fourteen months stale.

title: Grant acquittal shortfall
case_study: A community organisation acquitted a 400,000 grant with 380,000 of documented spend. The gap is attributed to in-kind volunteer labour valued at an internal rate never agreed with the funder. The deed permits in-kind contribution but is silent on valuation method.

title: Rolling outage after failover test
case_study: A scheduled failover test caused a four-hour partial outage. Failover succeeded in 90 seconds; the outage came from failback, where stale connection pools in three downstream services held references to the retired primary. The runbook does not mention failback.

title: Procurement single-source justification
case_study: A 1.2M software renewal was approved single-source on the ground that migration cost exceeded the price delta. The migration estimate came from the incumbent vendor and was not independently reviewed. Two competitors were not approached; the renewal lapses in nineteen days.

title: Payroll rounding drift
case_study: A payroll engine rounded superannuation contributions down to the nearest cent per line rather than per payment, understating employer contributions by an average of 3.40 per employee per fortnight across 4,100 staff for nineteen months.

title: Access reviews signed without evidence
case_study: Quarterly access reviews for a core banking system were certified complete for six consecutive quarters. The review tool exported an empty entitlement list for one business unit throughout, and every certification was a bulk approve with no exceptions raised.

title: Shadow reporting spreadsheet
case_study: A regulatory return has been assembled for three years in a spreadsheet maintained by one analyst, sourcing figures from a warehouse view that was deprecated eighteen months ago. The view still returns rows. The analyst resigned last week.

title: Vendor breach notification delay
case_study: A SaaS vendor disclosed a credential-stuffing incident 41 days after detection. The contract requires notification within 72 hours of detection. The vendor asserts the clock started at confirmed exfiltration, not at detection of anomalous access.

title: Uncalibrated sensor fleet
case_study: A water utility's chlorine sensors have exceeded their calibration interval by an average of seven months across 240 units. Readings remain within plausible bounds and no compliance breach has been recorded, which is itself the concern raised by the auditor.

title: Duplicate patient identifiers
case_study: A hospital merger produced 3,900 patient records with duplicate identifiers across the two source systems. The merge rule kept the most recently updated record, silently discarding allergy annotations held only on the older one.

title: Expense policy exception creep
case_study: Exceptions to the travel expense policy rose from 4% to 31% of claims over two years. Each exception is individually approved by a delegate within authority. No review has assessed whether the policy or the pattern of exceptions is the outlier.

title: Backup restore never tested
case_study: Nightly backups of a case-management system have completed successfully for four years. No restore has ever been attempted. The retention policy was changed twenty months ago to exclude attachments, and the change is recorded only in a ticket comment.

title: Conflicted panel member
case_study: A tender evaluation panel member holds shares in the parent company of the winning bidder, disclosed on the conflict register but after scoring closed. The panel chair recorded the disclosure and did not re-run the evaluation.

title: Legacy interface silent truncation
case_study: An interface between a claims system and its downstream ledger truncates description fields at 40 characters without error. Reconciliation matches on amount and date only, so the truncation has never surfaced in a control report.

title: Overdue remediation actions
case_study: Of 61 internal audit actions rated high, 44 are past their agreed due date, with an average overrun of 214 days. Each has been formally extended at least once. No extension has been declined in the period reviewed.

title: Test data in production
case_study: A performance test seeded 12,000 synthetic customer records into the production database in a maintenance window. The cleanup script matched on an email domain that 38 real customers also use. Those records were deleted.

title: Delegation register out of date
case_study: The financial delegation register has not been reconciled against the identity system since a restructure fourteen months ago. Nine people who changed roles retain their prior approval limits, three of them upward.

title: Third-party library end of life
case_study: A payment tokenisation library reached end of support eleven months ago. It is embedded in four services, two of which have no owning team following a reorganisation. A CVE affecting it was published six weeks ago.

title: Incomplete incident timeline
case_study: A major incident review reconstructed the timeline from chat logs because the monitoring platform's retention is seven days and the review began on day nine. Three of the eleven contributing factors are attributed on recollection alone.

title: Consent records not migrated
case_study: A marketing platform migration carried across contact records but not the consent timestamps that justify contacting them. The vendor advises consent can be inferred from the presence of the record. 61,000 contacts are affected.
